title: Notable AI papers in the 2026-10-23 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This inferred ordering uses weak, mixed attention signals and demonstrated relevance; citation evidence is limited because the papers are newly announced.

sections.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an executable benchmark of paired safe/unsafe tasks across six domains to measure how tool-using agents behave when safety-relevant evidence is omitted and whether they recover it appropriately.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that omission robustness and useful evidence recovery are distinct: recovery access reduced unsafe execution across the ten evaluated models, while models differed in whether they sought and used the missing facts.
sections.unique_caveat: Results come from this benchmark’s six domains and evaluated model set; the authors note that the tested model profiles do not establish general deployment behavior.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Search surfaced a dedicated secondary overview and an explainer; the paper is cross-listed in two core AI categories.

sections.title: AgentPhishing: A Benchmark of LLM Email Agents Under Adaptive Attack
sections.abstract: The paper introduces an adaptive-phishing benchmark and attack-generation method to test whether LLM email agents detect persuasive phishing and refrain from complying with malicious requests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that agents safe on pre-existing phishing emails can remain vulnerable to adaptive, persuasive attacks; in their nine-agent evaluation, four had detection below 10% and malicious-request compliance above 45%.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit the evaluation to synthetic single-message attacks and selected configurations; scores cover decisions and drafted replies, not externally executed harm.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Search surfaced an AI-security digest and independent paper summaries; its cross-list connects security and core AI.

sections.title: When Is a Memory Safe Enough to Act On? Action-Conditioned Verification for Long-Lived Agents
sections.abstract: The authors formulate action-conditioned memory verification and propose a gate that decides which remembered facts to re-check, proceed, or abstain on based on the planned action and its consequences.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that AMV-Guard lowers verification cost on ToolSandbox while retaining safe-proceed recall, and lowers cost in a transfer evaluation with a small reduction in recall and task success.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper explicitly says premise extraction is model-driven, planning is bounded to a shallow lookahead, and the simulators omit some real-world consequences; scalability and broader action-class results remain unreported.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Search surfaced multiple paper-specific reviews/summaries; the work offers a concrete decision formulation and reports tests on ToolSandbox plus a gate-core transfer to AppWorld.

sections.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
sections.abstract: The paper proposes pruning partial reasoning traces by directly maximizing the chance that at least one retained trace completes correctly, thereby balancing trace quality and diversity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that their pass@$k$ objective outperforms the evaluated quality-only and diversity-only pruning baselines, especially when a moderate number of candidates is continued.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the eight evaluated open-weight models and tested pruning settings; the abstract does not establish gains across all reasoning tasks or inference systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Several search-indexed technical summaries discuss the method; the paper is cross-listed in AI and language and reports comparisons across eight open-weight reasoning models.

sections.title: AgenticEvolve: Evolutionary Program Search with Persistent Language Model Agents that Design and Run Experiments
sections.abstract: The authors replace one-shot evolutionary candidate generation with persistent LLM agents that run experiments between evaluations, reporting improved program-search results on heuristic-design and equation-discovery tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report better programs than No-analysis and OpenEvolve on two heuristic tasks, reaching baseline quality with fewer evaluations, and recovering more ground-truth structures on twelve equation-discovery problems.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is confined to the described heuristic and equation-discovery suites and three LLMs; broader scientific-search performance is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Search surfaced paper-specific summaries; it spans three core AI categories and compares the agent’s experimentation loop with an otherwise matched no-analysis configuration.

sections.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a training-free representation-alignment metric and report that it correlates with downstream robot task success, proposing it as a low-cost filter before closed-loop evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim that sensorimotor alignment can prioritize embodied models and VLM backbones before costly closed-loop rollouts or VLA fine-tuning.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports correlation, not a causal guarantee or replacement for closed-loop testing; model selection still requires downstream validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three core categories spanning vision, learning, and robotics, and addresses a practical evaluation-cost bottleneck.

sections.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
sections.abstract: The authors embed a low-frequency image trace throughout a dataset and detect it in generated outputs to audit whether a text-to-image model used that collection for fine-tuning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report high detection rates under their evaluated transformations and datasets while preserving image similarity, with removal under their strongest tested adaptive attack causing substantial FID degradation.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported robustness is bounded by the tested datasets, architectures, and adaptive attacks; it does not establish performance against every possible transformation or removal strategy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in vision and learning and reports multi-dataset and multi-transformation tests.

sections.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
sections.abstract: The authors study learned token-commitment policies for masked diffusion language models and propose trajectory-contraction targets that trade policy overhead against generation speed and accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report an improved accuracy–NFE frontier and throughput on GSM8K for their policy, with competitive results at moderate targets on MATH-500 and HumanEval and transfer to Dream-7B-Instruct.
sections.unique_caveat: The main reported result is on LLaDA-8B-Instruct, with transfer evidence to one additional model; the abstract does not establish broad model-family generality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The study compares teacher labels, policy inputs, and overhead and reports results on GSM8K, MATH-500, and HumanEval.
